propositions: The bridge is hard-wired to one tracker project at three points: JiraConfig.project scalar, fetcher JQL pair, and applier outbound mutation guard, preventing teams from syncing multiple tracker projects against a single codebase.

One shared ticket store should own the project set via a .bridge_state/projects.json mapping keyed by project→repos, with each ingested ticket recording its source project and configured repos, eliminating per-repo project disagreement over shared snapshot state.

The ticket project field is tri-state (absent=legacy default, explicit-empty=never sync, explicit-key=sync there); migration seeds the mapping from Backend.project with zero events written, resolving absent projects against the recorded legacy default.

Multi-project inbound fetch must iterate the configured project set for base JQL AND all three enrichment passes (parent/comment/issuelink maps) separately, merging results keyed by issue into a single snapshot, with per-query truncation scoped per project.

The store-compat capability stamp must register multi-project-bridge as required when the mapping holds >1 project, written atomically with the mapping mutation in one tracker commit, causing older binaries lacking the capability to fail closed on multi-project stores.

Outbound dispatch must use per-ticket project on create rather than repo default, and the cross-project guard must relax from single configured project to set membership, while tickets with explicitly-empty project produce no mutations.
